'''''Acanthus spinosus''''', the '''spiny bear's breech''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Acanthaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern Europe, from Italy to western Turkey. It is an [[herbaceous]] [[perennial]] growing to {{convert|150|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|60|-|90|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide. The deeply cut leaves have spiny margins, and in early summer it bears erect, {{convert|1|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} long racemes of white flowers with maroon [[bract]]s.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|page=1136}}</ref>

It is thought that both ''A. spinosus'' and close relative ''[[Acanthus mollis|A. mollis]]'' were introduced to Britain from the Mediterranean by the [[Roman Empire]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20091028060850/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/3324985/How-to-grow-Acanthus.html How to grow: Acanthus – Telegraph<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> It has been intermittently cultivated ever since, and is now a regular feature of the [[herbaceous border]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/gardening/plants/plant_finder/plant_pages/6.shtml BBC – Gardening: Plant Finder – Bear's breeches<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>  For centuries, [[Acanthus (ornament)|stone or bronze stylized versions of acanthus leaves have appeared as decoration]] on certain styles of architecture and furniture.
